persona: Dr. Sarah Chen, RN-BSN, Clinical Education Coordinator at Metropolitan Hospital Center; 12 years nursing education experience; researcher looking to measure workshop effectiveness and symptom improvement over time.
source_style: Real workshop record (de-identified); nursing education literature standard for paired pre-test/post-test designs.

columns.name: Participant_ID
columns.notes: Sequential ID 1-28 for 28 registered nursing students in the workshop cohort.

columns.name: Attended
columns.notes: Actual Python boolean (True/False cells). 20 attended full workshop, 8 did not (attended only part-time or dropped).

columns.name: Result_Before
columns.notes: Pre-workshop clinical assessment result. Deliberately includes case/space variants: 'pass', 'PASS', 'Pass', 'Pass ', 'fail', 'Fail', 'FAIL' to test normalization.

columns.name: Result_After
columns.notes: Post-workshop clinical assessment result (8 weeks after). Same levels as Result_Before. Also includes variants: 'pass', 'PASS', 'Pass', 'Pass ', 'fail', 'Fail', 'Fail '. Paired with Result_Before for McNemar's test.

columns.name: Symptom_Visit1
columns.notes: Baseline clinic visit: presence of target symptom cluster (e.g., 'anxiety during patient handoff'). Yes=15, No=13.

columns.name: Symptom_Visit2
columns.notes: 4-week follow-up clinic visit: same symptom. Yes=13, No=15. Repeated measure for Cochran's Q.

columns.name: Symptom_Visit3
columns.notes: 8-week follow-up clinic visit: same symptom. Yes=12, No=16. Repeated measure for Cochran's Q across all 3 visits.

columns.name: Age
columns.notes: Participant age at workshop enrollment (27–55 years). Demographic covariate, not required for primary analyses.

columns.name: Experience_Years
columns.notes: Years of clinical nursing experience prior to workshop (1–20 years). Demographic context.

clean_table.description: What the 'correct' version would look like after naive cleaning

intended_analysis.primary_goal_1: McNemar's test for paired binary outcomes: does the workshop move participants from Fail→Pass (improvement)? Compare Result_Before vs Result_After.
intended_analysis.primary_goal_2: Cochran's Q test for repeated measures: is there a significant trend in symptom presence across 3 clinic visits (baseline, 4wk, 8wk)? Test H0: symptom probability constant across Visit1, Visit2, Visit3.
intended_analysis.secondary: Descriptive: attendance rate (20/28=71%), baseline symptom prevalence (15/28=54%), age/experience distribution.

mess_applied: Case variance: 'pass'/'PASS'/'Pass' vs 'fail'/'Fail'/'FAIL' in Result_Before and Result_After cells (8 distinct strings for 2 logical values). Tests whether the tool normalizes category labels before analysis.
Trailing space: 'Pass ' (with trailing space) appears in both columns; 'Fail ' appears in Result_After only. Naive string matching fails.
Attended as actual boolean (True/False cells, not strings 'TRUE'/'FALSE'). Tests whether the tool correctly identifies and preserves boolean type.
Row order: Participant_ID is SORTED 1..28 (verified from bytes; an earlier claim of random ordering was false).
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Counting distinct 'pass' vs 'PASS' as separate categories (8 categories instead of 2 for result columns). Inflates chi-square df.
Failing to normalize before McNemar test: computing 2×2 contingency table on all 8 variants separately, breaking the test structure.
Treating 'Pass ' (with space) as a separate level; missing concordant pairs that are semantically equivalent.
Misclassifying Attended as string 'True'/'False' instead of boolean, affecting filtering logic if the tool tries to subset(Attended==True).
Attempting Cochran's Q directly without recognizing that all three Symptom columns share the same (Yes/No) level set. Wrong test selection if treating them as independent.
Mixing attended and non-attended participants without stratification; symptom prevalence may be different by attendance, confounding the visit effect.
